topic: Massage for dancers' hips and feet

slides.headline: Long rehearsals, aching hips and arches?
slides.sub: Where remedial massage fits into a dancer's recovery week.

slides.title: Where dancers carry the load
slides.body: Turnout, jumps and hours on demi-pointe ask a lot of the deep hip muscles, calves and the small muscles under the foot. Tightness and fatigue there are common through a busy term.

slides.title: What massage can help with
slides.body: Many dancers find massage eases that heavy, tight feeling around the hips, calves and arches. It complements strength work, technique and rest rather than replacing them.

slides.title: Time it around rehearsals
slides.body: Lighter work tends to suit the day before a performance. Deeper work usually feels better on a lighter training day, so your legs have time to settle before a demanding class.

slides.title: Look after your feet at home
slides.body: Roll your arch on a ball for a minute, do slow calf raises through full range, and practise spreading your toes while seated. Small daily habits add up over a season.

slides.title: When to see a physio
slides.body: Pain on top of the foot that builds with jumping, a hip that clicks with pain, or an ankle that won't settle after a landing is worth a physio assessment. Our team can refer you across.

slides.headline: Hips and feet need some care?
slides.body: Our remedial massage therapists work through your hips, calves and feet to support recovery between classes and rehearsals. Book online — link in bio.

caption:
New term, more rehearsals, and your hips and arches are already letting you know. 🩰

Turnout, jumps and time on demi-pointe load the deep hip muscles, calves and feet. Many dancers find remedial massage helps those areas feel less tight and heavy through a busy term.

Massage sits alongside strength work, good technique and rest, not instead of them. Keep deeper sessions for lighter days, and look after your feet at home with a ball, slow calf raises and toe spreading. Pain on top of the foot that builds with jumping or an ankle that won't settle is worth a physio assessment.

Our remedial massage therapists at Hybrid Physiotherapy work closely with our physios. Book online via the link in bio.
